comments.body: ## Client diversity We may need to campaign large stakers (again) to improve client diversity. The numbers **may not be accurate**. Lighthouse appears to be increasing. We also need better numbers. *From: https://clientdiversity.org/#distribution* *From: https://dune.com/hildobby/eth2-staking* #### Lido (Q3) > Lighthouse and Vouch each account for roughly a quarter of all Curated Module validators (26.70% and 22.59%, respectively, with minor quarterly variation). *From: https://blog.lido.fi/lido-validator-and-node-operator-metrics-q3-2025/#curated-module-consensus-client-diversity* #### Coinbase (February) > Our ETH validators support: > * Consensus clients: Lighthouse, Prysm > * Execution clients: Geth, Nethermind > * Looking forward: We are currently evaluating the production readiness of two more implementations and plan to continue expanding our client diversity. > > Lighthouse: 19.8%; Prysm 80.2% *From: https://www.coinbase.com/en-au/blog/ethereum-validator-performance-report*

## Naming

* Portmanteau needed for [Heka + Bogotá](https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/portmanteau-for-heka-bogota-upgrade-after-glamsterdam/26400): Hektá & Hekotá leading the signaling, but ACD can choose how they like.  
Note: @leobago wants[ Heka removed as the H-star name](https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/h-star-name-for-consensus-layer-upgrade-after-glamsterdam/24298/10) as it isn't in the IAU catalog.
* [Mascot](https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/mascot-needed-for-glamsterdam-upgrade/26008) needed for Glamsterdam. 🐜 🐝 🦩 🐩.   Yes really, there is even [EIP-8066](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8066) for upgrade mascots.
* [I-star name](https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/i-star-name-for-consensus-layer-upgrade-after-heka/26717) stars wanted.  Yes it may feel early, but if Glamsterdam targets June 2026, then the I-star headliner process could be happening at this time.

### [EIP-8081](https://forkcast.org/upgrade/hekota/): Hardfork Meta - Heka/Bogotá

We should first define the **Fork Focus** and then converge towards **Headliner(s)** as per the [process](https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/community-consensus-fork-headliners-acd-working-groups/24088), rather than skip ahead to choosing a headliner. 

Once Glamsterdam scoping is done (hopefully by December), we can focus on the following:
1. **Retro** on Fusaka (and update any processes based on that) ([retro](https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/2025-upgrade-process-retrospective/27082) on Eth Magicians)
2. Define **[Fork Focus](https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/community-consensus-fork-headliners-acd-working-groups/24088#p-58740-defining-the-fork-focus-4)** for Heka/Bogotá 
3. Converge on **Headliner(s)** for Heka/Bogotá (hopefully by late January / early February to give enough time to ideally ship two 6 monthly upgrades in 2026)

### **Staking Liquidity EIP-8061 and EIP-6914**
Hello, I currently lead research and trading for Fidelity's digital asset management division and would like to offer my perspective for prioritizing upcoming upgrades. These proposals allow for improved capital efficiency and risk balancing for stakers. I recognize blockchain mechanics and design trade-offs are complex and value this community's thoughtfulness in building a secure global settlement layer for assets. Please find my full comment here: https://github.com/pLangOnchain/Ethereum-EIP-Comments/issues/1.

- Institutional asset managers are keen on incorporating diversified sources of yield for client portfolios. 
- A primary obstacle for institutional adoption of Ethereum staking is the significant illiquidity risk, with combined entry and exit queue delays reaching approximately 70 days at the end of October, which is incompatible with traditional financial products.
- I recommend the Ethereum Foundation consider an increase in the churn limit (EIP-8061), increasing withdrawal slots, recycling validator indices (EIP-6914), and enabling bundled distributed deposits to improve liquidity and efficiency.

Hi all, Lighthouse have prepared a team opinion on trustless payments [here](https://blog.sigmaprime.io/lighthouse-trustless-payments.html). 

The short version is that the majority of our team support its continued inclusion, however we note a significant minority opinion that would prefer we delay its inclusion to the next fork. This would let us spend time ensuring the design is right and all implementation complexities properly understood.
Congratulations ACDC, we now have a star named Heka. Bonus, it's apparently visible from Bogota.
